history.title: History
history.description: The origin and evolution of Goju Ryu Karate
history.origins-desc: Goju-Ryu karate was developed in Okinawa, Japan in the early 20th century by Chojun Miyagi. The name 'Goju' comes from the 'hard-soft' principle of traditional Chinese martial arts and reflects the dual nature of the system: it combines hard striking techniques with softer, circular movements for both offense and defense.
history.development-desc: The growth and spread of Goju Ryu across the globe
history.lineage-desc: The key teachers and their contributions to the style

subsections.early-history-desc: The roots of Goju Ryu trace back to Chinese martial arts and their integration into Okinawan culture.
subsections.miyagi-era-desc: Chojun Miyagi's development and systematization of the Goju Ryu style in the 1920s and 1930s.
subsections.post-war-desc: The spread and evolution of Goju Ryu after World War II.
subsections.modern-era-desc: The contemporary development and global dissemination of Goju Ryu.

history.timelineDescription: A fuller chronology built from the origins, masters, post-war rebuilding and modern development of Goju Ryu.

timelineEvents.title: Fuzhou roots
timelineEvents.description: The roots of Goju Ryu are linked to Chinese martial arts in Fuzhou, especially the teachings associated with Ryu Ryu Ko.

timelineEvents.title: Kanryo Higaonna is born
timelineEvents.description: Kanryo Higaonna is born in Nishimura, Naha, the future bridge between Chinese quanfa and Okinawan Naha-te.

timelineEvents.title: A turning point for Higaonna
timelineEvents.description: After the death of his father, Kanryo Higaonna's search for deeper martial training becomes more urgent.

timelineEvents.title: Training in China begins
timelineEvents.description: Higaonna travels to Fuzhou and trains for many years under Ryu Ryu Ko, building the foundation of what would later shape Goju Ryu.

timelineEvents.title: Return to Okinawa
timelineEvents.description: Higaonna returns to Naha and begins transmitting the Chinese methods he learned, adapted to Okinawan practice.

timelineEvents.title: Chojun Miyagi is born
timelineEvents.description: Chojun Miyagi is born in Naha and will later systematize the style as Goju Ryu.

timelineEvents.title: Miyagi becomes Higaonna’s student
timelineEvents.description: After earlier training with Ryuko Aragaki, Miyagi is introduced to Kanryo Higaonna and begins serious Naha-te training.

timelineEvents.title: Karate enters school life
timelineEvents.description: Higaonna teaches at the Naha Commercial School, helping bring Naha-te into a more public educational setting.

timelineEvents.title: Higaonna dies; Miyagi studies in China
timelineEvents.description: Kanryo Higaonna dies. Miyagi travels to Fuzhou to research the Chinese roots of his teacher’s art.

timelineEvents.title: Public recognition grows
timelineEvents.description: Miyagi demonstrates karate for Crown Prince Hirohito, raising the visibility of Okinawan karate.

timelineEvents.title: Training method matures
timelineEvents.description: Miyagi develops Junbi Undo and creates Tensho, giving the system clearer preparation, breathing and soft circular principles.

timelineEvents.title: Karate research clubs form
timelineEvents.description: Miyagi helps organize research groups in Okinawa to study, preserve and refine karate across styles.

timelineEvents.title: The name Goju Ryu is chosen
timelineEvents.description: After Jinan Shinzato is asked to name the style, Miyagi chooses Goju Ryu from the hard-soft principle in the Bubishi.

timelineEvents.title: Official recognition in Japan
timelineEvents.description: Goju Ryu is registered and recognized through the Dai Nippon Butokukai, giving the style formal standing.

timelineEvents.title: Miyagi teaches abroad
timelineEvents.description: Miyagi serves as an Okinawan representative and spends eleven months teaching karate in Hawaii.

timelineEvents.title: Research trip to Shanghai
timelineEvents.description: Miyagi visits Shanghai to deepen his research into Chinese martial arts and their connection to his karate.

timelineEvents.title: Kyoshi title awarded
timelineEvents.description: The Dai Nippon Butokukai awards Miyagi the Kyoshi title, confirming his status as a leading karate teacher.

timelineEvents.title: Morio Higaonna is born
timelineEvents.description: Morio Higaonna is born in Naha and later becomes one of the most influential transmitters of traditional Goju Ryu.

timelineEvents.title: War losses
timelineEvents.description: World War II devastates Okinawa. Miyagi loses students, family members and many training notes and documents.

timelineEvents.title: An’ichi Miyagi starts training
timelineEvents.description: An’ichi Miyagi begins training under Chojun Miyagi and becomes closely connected to his final years of teaching.

timelineEvents.title: The dojo rebuilds
timelineEvents.description: New students return to training after the war, with An’ichi Miyagi increasingly supporting technical instruction.

timelineEvents.title: Chojun Miyagi dies
timelineEvents.description: Chojun Miyagi dies. Eiichi Miyazato takes responsibility for the dojo, while An’ichi Miyagi continues the technical teaching.

timelineEvents.title: Morio Higaonna enters the dojo
timelineEvents.description: Morio Higaonna officially joins the dojo and trains intensively under An’ichi Miyagi.

timelineEvents.title: Okinawan organization and Jundokan
timelineEvents.description: The Okinawa Karate-do Renmei is founded, and the Jundokan dojo becomes an important center for Goju Ryu practice.

timelineEvents.title: Training continues across distance
timelineEvents.description: An’ichi Miyagi leaves Okinawa for work, while Morio Higaonna moves to Tokyo and continues training whenever he returns.

timelineEvents.title: All-style dan examinations
timelineEvents.description: At the Okinawan all-style dan examinations, Morio Higaonna is promoted to sandan.

timelineEvents.title: Tetsuji Nakamura is born
timelineEvents.description: Tetsuji Nakamura is born in Osaka and later becomes a major international Goju Ryu teacher.

timelineEvents.title: IOGKF is founded
timelineEvents.description: Morio Higaonna founds the International Okinawan Goju-Ryu Karate-do Federation to preserve and spread traditional Goju Ryu worldwide.

timelineEvents.title: Return to Okinawa
timelineEvents.description: Higaonna returns to Okinawa, opens a dojo and appears in the BBC series The Way of the Warrior.

timelineEvents.title: International links deepen
timelineEvents.description: Higaonna promotes Goju Ryu in the United States and visits Fuzhou repeatedly, strengthening links with Chinese martial arts circles.

timelineEvents.title: Nakamura chooses the traditional path
timelineEvents.description: Tetsuji Nakamura wins the IOGKF World Championship in free fighting and commits himself to traditional Goju Ryu.

timelineEvents.title: Shudokan is founded
timelineEvents.description: Nakamura establishes Shudokan as a base for traditional Goju Ryu training.

timelineEvents.title: An’ichi Miyagi dies
timelineEvents.description: An’ichi Miyagi dies, leaving a lasting legacy through the students who preserved Chojun Miyagi’s later teachings.

timelineEvents.title: New Shudokan dojo in Canada
timelineEvents.description: Nakamura opens a new Shudokan dojo in Canada, strengthening his international teaching base.

timelineEvents.title: The flame is passed on
timelineEvents.description: Morio Higaonna passes responsibility for carrying the tradition forward to Tetsuji Nakamura.
